answer: Four design axes were available. (1) Audit blob handling: gitignore (chosen) vs BFG/git-filter-repo history scrub vs structured audit-emit to oya-audit-chain-domain (the latter exists as a real crate triad: oya-audit-chain-domain/usecase/file-adapter at crates/). Chosen approach masks the architectural defect — agent-read events bypassed the canonical audit sink and were dumped to a freeform .jsonl. Gitignore prevents recurrence of the symptom but not the root cause (agents still write to .audit/ instead of the chain). (2) Dir move: bundling gitignore+move+ADR (chosen) is acceptable for CC-2 hygiene PRs but masks that the gitignore work and the topology move share no domain; a split would have made `git revert` of either independently cheap. The bundled PR is non-trivial to bisect if any of the 7 rewritten path refs proves stale. (3) Argo path strategy: hardcoded `const ARGO_MANIFEST` (chosen, line 257) vs env-derived vs CRD-lookup. The const is the third time this string moves; a config-derived path (e.g. read from a known infra-topology.json or env var with default) would have made this PR a 1-line change next time. Masked trade-off: every future infra-topology consolidation re-triggers a multi-file rewrite + ADR. (4) ADR pattern: per-move ADR-0117 (chosen) is appropriate for the first consolidation, but absent an umbrella infra-topology ADR establishing `infra/kyverno/` as THE admission root (vs `deploy/gitops/` as deprecated), future agents lack the principle and may reintroduce sprawl. The chosen bundle is pragmatic for CC-2 but leaves two principle-shaped gaps: structured audit emission and infra-topology canonicalization.
alternatives_considered: Audit blob: gitignore (chosen) — cheap, addresses symptom only
Audit blob: git-filter-repo to scrub the 52KB jsonl from history — heavyweight, justified only if blob contained secrets (it does not)
Audit blob: route agent-read events to oya-audit-chain-domain (existing crate) — addresses root cause; out of scope for hygiene PR but should be a follow-up
Dir move: bundled with gitignore + ADR (chosen) — pragmatic for CC-2, harder bisect
Dir move: split into 2 PRs (gitignore alone; move + ADR alone) — cleaner revert boundary, ~2x PR overhead
Dir move: deferred batched topology PR consolidating all infra/* roots at once — best long-term, but blocks current Argo work
Argo path: hardcoded const (chosen, tools/.../main.rs:257) — simple, fragile to future moves
Argo path: env var with default (e.g. OYA_ARGO_MANIFEST) — survives moves without code change
Argo path: config-derived from infra-topology.json — single source of truth, larger upfront
Argo path: CRD lookup via kubectl get application — runtime correctness but adds K8s dep to gate app
ADR pattern: per-move ADR-0117 (chosen) — narrow, repeats per consolidation
ADR pattern: umbrella infra-topology ADR declaring infra/kyverno/ canonical + deploy/gitops/ deprecated — preventive, requires more council deliberation
key_claims: oya-audit-chain-domain crate triad exists (crates/oya-audit-chain-domain, -usecase, -file-adapter); .audit/agent-read.jsonl bypassed it — symptom-only fix masks the routing defect

ARGO_MANIFEST is hardcoded at tools/oya-vcs-provider-execution-gate-app/src/main.rs:257 and re-referenced at kernel src/lib.rs (3 hits per ADR); third location-change for the same string is plausible within the year
infra/kyverno/ is asserted as canonical in ADR-0117 narrative but no umbrella infra-topology ADR codifies the rule for the next agent
Bundled 9-file PR with 7 path rewrites + ADR + gitignore is bisect-hostile if any evidence/multispectrum JSON ref later proves to need different rewrite semantics
ADR explicitly notes one ref (evidence/multispectrum/...-1778845600.json) was not in the prior agent's enumeration — suggests rewrite enumeration is artisanal, not lane-enforced
uncertainty_areas: Whether oya-audit-chain-domain is wired to receive agent-read events today or is only domain scaffolding (would change the severity of the audit-routing alternative)
Whether an umbrella infra-topology ADR was rejected explicitly or simply not considered
Whether ARGO_MANIFEST has moved before (history-traceable but not inspected here)
Whether deploy/gitops/ retains other intended uses (ADR claims it was single-file but no grep evidence in diff)

findings.summary: Symptom-only fix for .audit/ blob — agent-read events still emit to filesystem jsonl rather than canonical oya-audit-chain-domain sink
findings.recommended_action: Open follow-up to route agent-read events through oya-audit-chain-usecase; gitignore stays as belt-and-suspenders

findings.summary: ARGO_MANIFEST hardcoded in 4+ locations; third path-move for same string would re-trigger multi-file rewrite + ADR
findings.recommended_action: Refactor to env-var with default (OYA_ARGO_MANIFEST) or read from a future infra-topology.json; track as P3

findings.summary: No umbrella infra-topology ADR establishes infra/kyverno/ as the canonical admission root; next agent may reintroduce parallel root
findings.recommended_action: Promote ADR-0117 narrative paragraph into a standalone infra-topology ADR (or supersede ADR-0117 with one) declaring deploy/gitops/* deprecated

findings.summary: Bundled PR (gitignore + move + ADR) is acceptable for CC-2 but bisect-hostile; consider splitting future hygiene bundles
findings.recommended_action: Document a CC-2 bundling heuristic: bundle only if both halves share rollback semantics

findings.summary: Rewrite enumeration was artisanal (one ref missed by prior agent's grep); no lane enforces 'all path-string refs rewritten on git mv'
findings.recommended_action: Consider a path-ref-integrity lane that flags hardcoded path strings to renamed/moved dirs
